title: reverse-mentorship-ask-lane-1on1-notes-zoe-hart-may04-2026
content:
Purpose and quick framing:
- Goal for this 1:1: Ask Lane to try a reverse-mentorship experiment and get explicit buy-in. I want to transfer a bit of frontend performance / React Suspense debugging know-how to him so he can better unblock cross-team prioritization and advocacy when we ask infra changes.
- Secondary: surface career asks (path to Staff Eng lead on infra-adjacent projects) and align on how Lane can sponsor/advocate in syncs with leadership.

Meeting logistics:
- Duration: 30 min (tight)
- Format: 10m check-in + 10m reverse-mentorship ask + 10m career + quick actions
- Prep for Lane: None required, but I will bring a short demo sandbox and 2 examples that illustrate why manager-level familiarity matters for our roadmap decisions.

Agenda (script + prompts):
1) Quick personal check-in (2–3m)
   - How's the week? Triage energy level (S/M/L)
   - One quick highlight I want to celebrate: cross-team rollout of continuous KV cache (shipped last week) — shout out to Lane for clearing infra quota blockers.

2) Reverse-mentorship proposal (8–10m)
   - Why: Observed a few times where leadership decisions (capacity allocation, model routing priority) were deferred because managers weren't confident about frontend perf implications. If you (Lane) had a 1:1 baseline of the debugging model, you could: 1) ask better clarifying questions in exec syncs, 2) reduce handoffs, 3) unblock engineers faster.
   - The ask (concrete): Run a monthly 30–45m slot where I lead a short walkthrough of one real perf incident + 1 targeted toolkit skill (e.g., React Suspense traces, bundle-splitting for streaming). We also do a 15m shadow session every other month where you observe me pair-debugging an incident.
   - Benefits for Lane: faster context for prioritization, better judgment calls on Dedicated capacity tradeoffs, higher credibility in cross-functional dialogs.
   - Commitments I’m offering: prepare a 10–12 slide mini-deck + 15-min live demo, maintain a short FAQ doc, and propose 2 small homework items after each session (watch a 10m screencast, try an introspective question in your next sync).

3) Career / sponsorship focused ask (6–8m)
   - Progress snapshot: Lead on KV cache rollout, mentorship of 2 ICs, running postmortems. Goals: move to Principal/Staff stretch (lead infra-adjacent project, own cross-team contract with serving runtime).
   - Ask: Would Lane be open to 1) surface me as candidate for the Platform owner slot in the next product sync (May 20 planning), and 2) provide a short note on current strengths and gaps that I can use in my self-eval?
   - Evidence I’ll share: short bullet list of wins + lessoned learnings (I’ll drop into this doc after meeting).

4) Blockers and quick tactical items (2–3m)
   - Current blockers: PR blocking api-gateway rollback policy (see PR link), lack of dedicated time for cross-team testing (need a 2h recurring slot with runtime team).
   - Quick asks for Lane: help broach a 2-hour monthly cross-team testing slot with Runtime leads; escalate ENG-4227 priority if no response by May 10.

5) Action items and timeline (final 2m)
   - If Lane agrees to the reverse-mentorship experiment: set up recurring monthly slot: "Platform reverse-mentorship" (30–45m) starting first week of June. Owner: Zoe (create invite + mini-deck), Due: 2026-05-10 to seed calendar.
   - Shadow pairing: schedule 45m observation in May or June. Owner: Lane to accept invite.
   - Sponsorship ask: Lane to mention me as candidate at next product sync (May 20). Owner: Lane. By: 2026-05-20.
   - PR escalation: Lane to ping runtime leads on ENG-4227 and cc Priya. Owner: Lane. By: 2026-05-10.
   - I'll update this doc after the meeting with concrete feedback and the mini-deck link. Owner: Zoe. By: 2026-05-05.

Notes to self (talking points / scripts):
- When I say "reverse-mentorship," emphasize low overhead: short demos, tangible takeaways. Avoid framing as "teach-you-everything".
- Be explicit about reciprocity: propose a 10m catch-up post-session where Lane shares what changed in his decisions as a result.
- If Lane hesitates on time, offer an asynchronous path: record a 12-min demo + 3 FAQs.

Unresolved / TBD:
- Will leadership accept nomination for Platform owner slot? (TBD after product sync)
- Calendar time: confirm Lane's weekly blocks — check Slack #calendar-ping.

Links / evidence to drop in if asked quickly:
- Live demo sandbox repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/perf-sandbox
- Perf incident example: PR #432 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/432) — contains trace captures and proposed hotfix.
- Jira ticket for PR dependency: JIRA-ENG-4227
- Confluence draft: confluence:PLATFORM-knowledge-sharing-2026

After-meeting checklist (what I'll do right away):
- Capture Lane's initial reaction and commitments into this doc (update by EOD).
- Draft the first mini-deck (6–10 slides) and upload to platform shared folder; link back here.
- Create calendar invite for the monthly slot and add required attendees.
- Follow up on PR escalation and confirm with Priya.

Tone notes: keep it collaborative, pragmatic, and specific. Avoid sounding like I'm asking for a promotion right away — frame sponsorship as helping me take on more cross-team responsibility.

Quick TL;DR (for subject line or Slack ping): "1:1 today — propose monthly reverse-mentorship (short demos + shadowing) so management has concrete frontend perf context; also ask for light sponsorship for Platform owner slot. Will bring 10-min demo and 2 examples."

End of doc.
